_comment: HW-ASSUME ledger — the firmware-side hardware-assumption inventory. TRUST_ASSUMPTIONS.md's §Out-of-scope explicitly EXCLUDES firmware; this file is the hole that leaves. Every row is a claim about silicon we did not design and cannot inspect, so unlike AXIOM_STATUS.json there is NO machine truth to check a row against — no `#print axioms` for a die. What `make verify-hw-assumptions` CAN falsify is everything around the premise: that each row's anchors still resolve, that each named make-target exists, and — the load-bearing one, borrowed from OpenTitan's bidirectional RTL<->Hjson countermeasure cross-check — that the set of HW-ASSUME ids in the ledger is EXACTLY the set referenced across the tree. A row nobody cites is dead; a citation with no row is an unledgered assumption. See docs/verification/hardware-assumption-boundary-2026-07-17.md §6.

_status_vocabulary.bare-tcb: Asserted; discharged by nothing but vendor prose. Zero assurance. The point of a row at this status is that it is NAMED.
_status_vocabulary.vendor-doc: Stated in an ST/Infineon/NXP reference manual or datasheet we have read and cited to a section.
_status_vocabulary.cert-cited: Covered by a third-party lab evaluation whose scope we have checked and recorded. An attestation of bounded expert effort — NOT a proof. EUCLEAK is the standing refutation: ~80 evaluations at the highest attack-potential rating missed a 14-year constant-time defect.
_status_vocabulary.silicon-tested: A positive test on OUR parts. Bounds disbelief; never a forall.
_status_vocabulary.code-enforced: The firmware fails closed if the premise is violated in an observable way. Does not make the premise true — it makes a violation detectable.

_falsifying_test_rule: Every row MUST carry a falsifying_test whose `description` states a concrete experiment that could FAIL. `exists: false` is honest and common; `exists: true` REQUIRES a make_target that the gate checks is real. A model earns assurance only in proportion to what could contradict it — a row with no falsifying test is prose in JSON.

assumptions.statement: An STM32U585 flash/OTP quad-word program is old-or-new under power loss; a torn quad-word is read-back-detectable or raises an ECC fault. A programmed quad-word cannot be re-driven (ECC is computed and latched over the whole 128-bit line at first program), including when the new data would only clear already-cleared bits.

evidence.anchor: STM32U5 flash does NOT allow re-
cannot re-program a bit that is already 0

falsifying_test.description: Power-cut rig on sacrificial U585s: cut VDD at swept sub-us offsets across a quad-word program and across a page erase; classify every read-back into old / new / ECC-fault / other. 'Other' falsifies. The recovery-LOGIC half needs zero new hardware (reset-at-swept-delay, work-todo C7); only the analog torn-write half needs a glitcher.
falsifying_test.cost: rig + sacrificial parts; the logic half is free
falsifying_test.procedure: docs/security/red-teaming.md §6.4 (Scaffold crowbar; reset-only half needs no glitcher; D4 torn-master sub-test)

consumed_by: invariant-2 (page-124 PIN attempt counter: one fresh blank QW per bump)
assumptions.note: The page-123 TLC pilot's FINDING 1 is exactly this premise: with torn=MayValid instead of torn=Skip the invariant is VIOLATED. So the pilot does not prove crash-atomicity; it proves crash-atomicity IS EQUIVALENT TO this hardware premise. That is the honest shape and it is why this row exists.

assumptions.statement: An OTP quad-word programmed once can never be re-driven, and a virgin quad-word is distinguishable from a programmed one by reading all-1s. A half-burn (one QW of a two-QW field programmed) is therefore detectable by a per-quad-word read.

evidence.anchor: An OTP quad-word may be programmed only once

falsifying_test.description: Half-program an OTP quad-word, attempt completion, record FLASH_SR PGSERR/WRPERR and the read-back. Needs NO sacrificial board: otp.rs maps 176..512 = 336 B = 21 UNALLOCATED quad-words, so ~21 independent shots fit on a board that stays usable (work-todo C8).
falsifying_test.cost: 2-3 d; ~21 shots on a still-usable board
falsifying_test.procedure: docs/security/red-teaming.md §6.4 (firmware reprogram-reject, no glitcher; ~21 shots/usable board)

consumed_by: secure/src/hw/otp.rs (device-master burn + the rejected rollback tally)
assumptions.note: The widely-cited ST community thread on stuck half-quad-words does NOT settle the mechanism: ST confirmed the issue and fixed it in STM32CubeProgrammer v2.19.0 while stating no root cause, and it concerns the host SWD programming path, not our firmware path. Do not cite it as silicon semantics in either direction. Note also that bit-level monotonicity being TRUE is not sufficient: the rejected unary rollback tally was built on exactly that true premise and was still invalid, because the binding constraint is quad-word-program-once. Model at the commit granularity.

assumptions.statement: An SE050 PUT KEY with P1=0x0B, P2=0x81 and three key blocks (ENC || MAC || DEK) replacing key-version-number 0x0B in place is ALL-OR-NOTHING across the SE's internal NVM commit.

evidence.anchor: Fresh link, then probe FINAL (resume / idempotence).

falsifying_test.description: Drive PUT KEY, cut power mid-APDU, then probe ENC/MAC and DEK INDEPENDENTLY. A die with final ENC/MAC but a transport DEK falsifies it. The probe must be independent because SCP03 establish proves ENC+MAC only.
falsifying_test.procedure: docs/security/red-teaming.md §5.7 (Scaffold crowbar on SE050 Vdd; independent ENC/MAC vs DEK probe)

consumed_by: secure/src/first_boot/state.rs (the Phase-B ceremony's SE050 key step)
CLAUDE.md ship gate 'atomic durable old/new/KVN recovery proof'
assumptions.note: THE worked example for the whole method. All three key blocks ride ONE APDU; the resume probe (establish_with(final_enc, final_mac)) proves ENC+MAC ONLY — the DEK is never probed — and the KVN is 0x0B before AND after, so it cannot disambiguate transport from final. If PUT KEY is atomic the probe is sound (one APDU). If it is not, ENC+MAC-final-with-DEK-still-transport is reachable, the probe reports 'already rotated -> resume', run() commits DONE_SE050_KEYS, and the device proceeds with a mixed keyset whose DEK is derived from the FACTORY-KNOWN transport root. Formalisation does not verify the SE050; it reduces a multi-thousand-line rotation path to this one sentence and tells you exactly which two values to probe.

assumptions.statement: The SE050 GP applet echoes the per-key KCVs in the PUT KEY (P1=0x0B, P2=0x81) response body, so a garbled/torn write is detectable at write time by comparing the returned KCVs against the expected key KCVs.

falsifying_test.description: On a sacrificial SE050, drive a successful transport->final PUT KEY and capture the decrypted response body length. body_len in {9,10} confirms KCVs are echoed; body_len == 0 means the applet returns no KCV.
falsifying_test.cost: sacrificial SE050 + logic analyzer on I2C2

assumptions.note: verify_put_key_response accepts a 0-length body as 'no KCV echoed' (accepted, since SW==0x9000 already confirmed the write) and verifies the {9,10}-byte KCV forms. If the bench shows KCVs ARE returned, the 0-length case becomes fail-closed. Until pinned, the KCV check catches torn/garbled writes only when the applet actually echoes KCVs; the DEK-liveness net (HW-ASSUME-PUTKEY-REPUT-IDEMPOTENT) covers the no-echo case.

assumptions.statement: The SE050 accepts an in-place GP PUT KEY (KVN 0x0B) that re-installs the identical final keys, so a DEK-liveness confirm (re-PUT of the final keys wrapped under the FINAL DEK) is a safe, idempotent probe that fails closed iff the on-chip DEK is not the final DEK.

falsifying_test.description: On a sacrificial SE050 already rotated to final keys, issue a second PUT KEY re-installing the identical final keys wrapped under the final DEK and read the status. Non-0x9000 falsifies idempotency (the safety net would then brick every first boot).

consumed_by: CLAUDE.md ship gate 'atomic durable old/new/KVN recovery proof'
assumptions.note: The DEK-liveness torn-write net is DELIBERATELY NOT shipped as live code until this confirms: it is a second in-place PUT KEY on every first boot, so if re-PUT-of-identical-keys is not accepted it would brick the flow. Pairs with HW-ASSUME-PUTKEY-ATOMIC (the irreducible atomicity question) and HW-ASSUME-PUTKEY-KCV-RESP.

assumptions.statement: SAES-CMAC(DHUK, .) produces identical output at RDP-1 and RDP-2 on the same die.

falsifying_test.description: Fingerprint one sacrificial die at RDP-1, self-lock to RDP-2, fingerprint again; divergence falsifies. One shot per part, irreversible.
falsifying_test.procedure: docs/security/red-teaming.md §6.5 (saes-self-test-hw fingerprint at RDP-1 vs after rdp2-self-lock; one-shot irreversible)

consumed_by: secure/src/first_boot/ (Phase A locks RDP-2, Phase B derives — both AT RDP-2)
assumptions.note: UNMEASURED, and no board in this project has ever been at RDP-2 — an RDP-2 part cannot be regressed, which is the entire point. ST prose ('SAES uses a constant instead of DHUK at RDP0; the real DHUK activates at RDP >= 1') implies RDP1 == RDP2; CLAUDE.md's 'only then [at RDP-2] is the per-die DHUK final' reads the other way. Both are consistent with everything measured (n=2 boards, RDP0 vs RDP1). The first-boot ceremony is self-consistent either way, so NO FUNCTIONAL TEST WILL EVER SURFACE THIS — only a deliberate probe can. If FALSE it is fail-secure for the downgrade route (the attacker computes f(DHUK_RDP1,salt) != PBS and both tunnels stay shut) but that consolation does NOT extend to a runtime TrustZone-M disable at RDP-2, which uses DHUK(RDP-2) directly.

assumptions.statement: DHUK is per-die and cannot be extracted into CPU-visible memory.

falsifying_test.description: Per-die: fingerprint more boards at RDP1 and require distinct outputs (n=2 today; a collision falsifies). Unextractability: decap, which is explicitly out of scope.
falsifying_test.cost: low for the per-die half; N/A for unextractability
falsifying_test.procedure: docs/security/red-teaming.md §6.5 (per-die fingerprint, n>=3 boards, no FI)

assumptions.note: Per-die: validated n=2 (two B-U585I boards give distinct RDP1 fingerprints; both share an ST constant at RDP0). Unextractability: bare-TCB. Say 'n=2, unmeasured at RDP2', never 'DHUK is unique per die' unqualified.

assumptions.statement: The Cortex-M33 CMSE instructions, SAU/IDAU attribution, and ST's GTZC peripheral behave as documented in ARM DDI0553 and ST RM0456.

evidence.anchor: proto NS_FLASH window escaped the SAU NS-flash region

falsifying_test.description: Extend the enforcement test per attribution rule. NO forall is reachable: there is no public formal ARMv8-M model in any framework, ARM's v8-M ASL was machine-validated (Reid, OOPSLA 2017) but never released, sail-arm is A-profile only, and GTZC is an ST peripheral that appears in NO ARM specification at all.

consumed_by: invariant-4 (all secrets only in TrustZone secure world)
assumptions.note: This surface is CLOSED, not backlog — the K tier is permanently unreachable absent an ARM release we do not control. The 7/7 RAZ-fault test is a positive test, not a forall, and it is nonetheless STRONGER evidence than the industry reference (Trusted Firmware-M) publishes for the same property. VERIFIED CAVEAT (work-todo C3, 2026-07-17): the receipt is taken on a NON-shipping feature combo. `ui-lcd = ["spi1-arduino", ...]` (secure/Cargo.toml), so the SHIPPING image secures SPI1 — the trusted-display bus — whereas `make gtzc-enforcement-hw` builds `ui-semihosting`, i.e. WITHOUT spi1-arduino, so its 7/7 RAZ-fault receipt runs against seccfgr2 == 0. The one bit that keeps NS off the trusted display is NOT covered by the enforcement test cited as evidence for it. Mitigated in the meantime by compile-time pins on all three TZSC images (sau.rs), mutation-checked: moving the I2C2 bit fails the build. Closing it needs the enforcement test rebuilt on the shipping combo.

assumptions.statement: The STM32U585 TRNG meets NIST SP 800-90B in our RNG_CR configuration, and its SECS/CECS status bits faithfully report its internal health-test failures.

evidence.anchor: const ERROR_FLAGS: u32 = SEIS | SECS | CEIS | CECS;

falsifying_test.description: CORRECTED 2026-07-17: not 'run SP 800-90B ourselves' (the U5 RNG exposes only conditioned output — no raw-noise API in the public HAL — so >=1e6 raw pre-conditioning samples are not cheaply obtainable). Instead: (a) confirm the firmware selects the CERTIFIED RNG config, not a candidate/custom one; (b) confirm E11's device coverage against its Public Use Document if ST publishes one, or accept the by-elimination read. See red-teaming.md §4.1 for the ESV Certificate #E11 provenance.
falsifying_test.procedure: docs/security/red-teaming.md §4.1 (RDP-0 raw-entropy dump -> SP 800-90B EA, no FI)

consumed_by: secure/src/crypto.rs (C10 keygen seeds, signing randomiser r, FI sentinels)
assumptions.note: CORRECTION 2026-07-17: an earlier version of this row (and hal/src/lib.rs) said 'no ESV certificate naming the U585 was found'. That was too strong. NIST ESV Entropy Certificate #E11 ('STM32U5x TRNG', Rev B, Physical noise source, SP 800-90B, validated 2022-12-16, UL Verification Services) exists; its Operating Environment is 'STM32U5x advanced Arm-based 32-bit MCU' and, by elimination of the later U5-subfamily certs (U5Fx/5Gx, U59x/5Ax, U535x/545x), it is the cert covering U585 — but E11 has NO published Public Use Document, so its exact device list is unenumerated. So: cert-cited by-elimination, not a confirmed U585 enumeration. Two residuals stand regardless: (1) E11 certifies the entropy SOURCE; whether OUR RNG_CR config is the certified one is a separate firmware check; (2) the public HAL exposes only CONDITIONED 32-bit output (no raw-noise API), so we cannot cheaply re-run 90B (which needs >=1e6 raw samples) on the production part. Firmware still fails closed on the RNG hardware health tests (SECS/CECS, work-todo D3), and rng_strong XOR-folds STM32+OPTIGA+SE050 on the irreversible paths.

assumptions.statement: STM32U585 readout protection level 2 resists voltage glitching and cannot be downgraded.

falsifying_test.description: Offensive FI campaign on sacrificial parts. High cost.
falsifying_test.procedure: docs/security/red-teaming.md §6.6.1 (FaultyCat EMFI µGlitch-shape + Scaffold voltage Šimoník-shape)

consumed_by: the evil-maid threat model (see the boundary doc §5)
assumptions.note: SESIP-2400133-01 (TrustCB, SGS Brightsight, SESIP3 + Physical Attacker Resistance, valid to 2027-03-28), ST security target TN1545 Rev 3, evaluated AT RDP-2 — real T-tier evidence, better than the absence argument. THREE caveats: (1) it pins REV_ID 0x3003 (rev U) and we probe DEV_ID only — see HW-ASSUME-REV-U; (2) we deliberately ship OUTSIDE the evaluated configuration — see HW-ASSUME-OEM2-ABSENT; (3) EUCLEAK's lesson applies unchanged. Independently: no published U5 RDP break exists, but U5 core-level glitch is PROVEN (Simonik, 76% PIN-check bypass on the STM32U5A9 sibling) and a TrustZone-M disable is PROVEN on the STM32L5 — a Cortex-M33 sibling (uGlitch, USENIX Sec 2023). This is the single highest-leverage unverifiable premise in the design, and it protects the attack class a hardware wallet actually faces.

assumptions.statement: Our STM32U585 dies are revision U (REV_ID 0x3003 at 0xE004_4002) — the only revision SESIP-2400133-01 / TN1545 Rev 3 covers.

falsifying_test.description: Boot any board and read the log: `hw::dbgmcu::report_die_id()` runs immediately after rcc::init() and prints dev_id/rev_id/rev/sesip_covered, shouting when the die is NOT the SESIP-covered rev U. Implemented 2026-07-17 (work-todo A4a); the probe reports and never faults, because a rev X/W part is good silicon that the certificate simply does not cover. REMAINING: nobody has yet RUN it on the bench dies and recorded the answer — that is the falsifying step, and it needs hardware.
falsifying_test.procedure: docs/security/red-teaming.md §3.3 (DONE: hw::dbgmcu boot probe, A4a) — bench step is boot-and-record

assumptions.note: Probe now EXISTS (secure/src/die_id.rs decode, host-tested incl. field-swap and wrong-part negatives; secure/src/hw/dbgmcu.rs one register read, base cross-checked against ST's CMSIS header by make verify-mmio-addresses). Before 2026-07-17 NO code read DBGMCU_IDCODE at all — every DEV_ID 0x482 check in this repo was a plan in a document. So the SESIP certificate was being cited on bench parts whose revision nobody had ever read. STILL UNCONFIRMED until someone boots a board and records the output: a rev X/W die is not a defect, it is simply outside SESIP-2400133-01's scope, and HW-ASSUME-RDP2's certificate evidence must not be cited for it.

assumptions.statement: No OEM2KEY is provisioned on a shipped unit and OEM2LOCK is clear, so no RDP-2 -> RDP-1 regression credential exists.

falsifying_test.description: Probe OEM1LOCK/OEM2LOCK on every unit at production test. Separately: probe whether any CubeIDE-touched bench board already carries ST's default OEM2 password (UM3387 reports CubeIDE's init script sets one) — that would be a live regression credential on our own bench. Low cost.
falsifying_test.procedure: docs/security/red-teaming.md §6.6 (option-byte OEM-lock read; CubeIDE default-password probe)

consumed_by: HW-ASSUME-RDP2 (this is WHY we ship outside the certified configuration)
assumptions.note: A DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE CERTIFIED CONFIGURATION, recorded so it is not silently inherited in either direction. TN1545:912 — 'In the certified configuration, the Integrator allows the platform to regress to RDP Level 1 when the TOE secret OEM2KEY is successfully provisioned, and the OEM2LOCK option bit is set.' TN1545:921 — 'If the Integrator sets RDP to Level 2 without programming the OEM2KEY the product is locked.' That locked state is exactly what lockdown.rs mandates, because a transit attacker could pre-plant an OEM2 password. We are STRICTER than the evaluated configuration for a documented threat-model reason — which also means the certificate's 'field return of platform' SFR does not hold for us (no RMA path). Collides with the OWNER-GATED provisioning-wipe-rma-authority surface.

assumptions.statement: Our SE050 parts are JCOP 4 SE050 v4.7 R2.00.11 / R2.03.11 — the configuration NSCIB-CC-180212-CR5 covers.

falsifying_test.description: Read the applet/config version off the part. Hours.

consumed_by: HW-ASSUME-SE-INTERNALS (the certificate is the only third-party evidence we have)
assumptions.note: UNCONFIRMED — the certificate covers nothing else. The SE050 cert is genuinely stronger than the OPTIGA one (its TOE includes the JCVM/JCRE/JCAPI, i.e. the layer enforcing our UserID PIN policy), but it explicitly does NOT rate cryptographic protocol strength, so it does not cover SCP03-as-deployed.

assumptions.statement: The OPTIGA Trust M and SE050 behave per datasheet inside the die: access-control policies are enforced, attempt counters are monotonic and durable, and lifecycle transitions are irreversible.

falsifying_test.description: None exists that reaches inside the die, and none will. Per-property silicon E2E on our own parts is the ceiling — each test can fail, which is what makes them worth running.
falsifying_test.cost: N/A for the general premise; low per property

assumptions.note: PERMANENTLY bare-TCB as a general premise. Every technique that could genuinely discharge it — firmware/RTL co-verification, OpenTitan-style FPV of a lifecycle controller, Termite's model-check-spec-against-RTL step — requires design source that Infineon and NXP will not supply. This is a business fact, not an effort estimate. Modelling SE internals is therefore theatre UNCONDITIONALLY: it relocates the assumption into a model we wrote and calls the agreement a proof. The gold standard here is make se050-admin-extract-attempt-e2e: a security claim + a test that fails if the policy regresses + a same-session DELETE as the control proving the refusal was real.
